failure_modes: Present-tense spiritual teaching and after-effect talk: 'create from a space of love', 'find that place of love and acceptance that we all hunger for' (5 passages)
Meditation, mystical practice or post-NDE re-entry into the state rather than the NDE itself ('energetically transform myself back into that space of love')
Third-party speculation about where the dead are: a reverend at a funeral, a father assumed to be 'in a place of peace'
A researcher/host generalising about what NDErs long for after they return
'place of knowing' during an unrelated psychic episode about a drowning child — same construction, different place
audits.suggested_regex: (?:I (?:was|found myself|awoke|woke up)|we were) (?:back )?(?:in|inside|surrounded by|immersed in) (?:this |that |a |an )?(?:place|space|state|realm) of (?:pure |absolute |total |complete |just )*(?:unconditional )?(?:love|peace|bliss|joy)

best_quote.text: And then all of a sudden, I was in this place of just pure unconditional love.

failure_modes: Host intros and channel boilerplate built on the phrase 'pre-birth memories' ('Max has both pre-birth memories and multiple near-death experiences') — 4 passages
Standalone pre-birth-memory guests who never describe an NDE; the plan is remembered from childhood, not from dying
'Soul contract' as an everyday spiritual belief: contracts with pets, contracts reported by astrologers, contracts figured out years later in therapy
Interviewer questions ('have you figured out your soul contract with him?')
A researcher summarising what experiencers in general report about soul contracts
audits.suggested_regex: (?:I (?:remembered|re-?remembered|was shown|was told|learned|realized|knew)|(?:he|she|they|god|my guide|the being)s? (?:told|showed) me)[^.]{0,80}(?:soul contract|planned (?:this|my) life|pre-?birth plan|chose (?:my|this) (?:parents|life)|agreed to (?:come|this))

best_quote.text: he told me that I had promised to give birth to him before I was born, that we had planned this together

failure_modes: The near-identical phrase 'I didn't know what to call it' applied to something else entirely — the NDE label, remote viewing, music therapy, the feeling of God (5 of the 8 false positives)
Ordinary-life disorientation: waking drugged in a foreign country, being trapped under lake ice, walking through your own house during a panic attack
Otherwise clean; the surviving matches are genuine in-experience hedges about location
audits.suggested_regex: (?:wherever I (?:was|had been)\b|I (?:didn't|did not|couldn't) know where I (?:was|had been|was going)\b)

best_quote.text: I knew I wasn't on earth anymore, and I didn't know where I was.

failure_modes: ELEVEN of 24 passages are the identical Roundtrip Death cold-open montage ('I didn't realize that was actually my physical body because I was somewhere else') replayed at the head of every episode — one clip inflating the account count by an order of magnitude
Geographic 'somewhere': 'somewhere in Asia' in a past-life meditation, 'somewhere in the Middle East' judged from people's dress
The medical setting: knowing you are 'somewhere else' on waking in a recovery room
Clock-time confusion in a gurney ('I knew I had been somewhere at 11:00 in the morning')
audits.suggested_regex: (?:I (?:kn[eo]w|realiz\w+|felt|was sure)(?: that)? I (?:was|had been|ended up) somewhere|the fact that I had been somewhere|I ended up somewhere)\b(?!\s+(?:in|between|at|near)\s)

best_quote.text: I didn't know where I was, but I knew that I was somewhere.

failure_modes: 'Purgatory' as Catholic doctrine rather than perceived terrain: childhood catechism, Medjugorje visionaries, indulgence arithmetic, 'there's nobody floating around in purgatory'
'Purgatory' as a theory about other souls — mediums describing clients, Monroe Institute speculation that belief systems can strand people
Earth itself called purgatory ('this is purgatory, and we've already lived it')
'Lost souls' as astral-plane instruction addressed to the listener in the second person
Documentary voiceover narrating a third party's hellish NDE
Content recovered in a hypnosis session rather than during the NDE

best_quote.text: They seemed to be stuck and very much in sorrow. Was this Purgatory? I do not know.

failure_modes: Idiomatic hell: 'everything went to hell', 'we've been to hell and back', slaughterhouse footage as 'hell on earth', domestic violence as 'I was in hell'
Doctrinal exposition with no experience attached — the six Buddhist realms, Calvinist eternal torment
Experiencers arguing hell does NOT exist and explaining away other people's hellish NDEs (3 passages)
Host bio intros and interviewer lines ('you called out to Jesus from the pit of hell', plus a book plug)
Someone else's NDE reported second-hand ('another person I spoke with told me she went to hell')
Being told online that you were in hell
audits.suggested_regex: (?:I (?:was|went|fell|was taken|was thrown|was dragged|was sent|ended up)(?: down)? (?:in|into|to) (?:a |the )?hell|I was in hell|(?:this|the|a) hell realm)\b(?! (?:on earth|and back))

best_quote.text: during that 10 minutes I went to hell and I remember enough to tell you that it was very very dark that I couldn't see my hand in front of my face

failure_modes: The defining feature — torment with NO imagery — has no lexical signature, so every candidate word ('despair', 'torment', 'hopeless', 'hell') is dominated by other things
Theological exposition about eternal conscious torment (Calvinism, end-times preaching) with no experience attached
Ordinary-life despair and biography: a precognitive dream, Christian guilt about tarot cards, a snowstorm walk, a custody hearing
Reaction-channel intros ('today we're going to watch a very scary hellish nde of a woman') and interviewer recaps
Distressing NDEs that DO have hellish scenery (pits, fire, mine-shafts) — the opposite of the claim
Passages where the answer is that there was NO despair ('there was no anguish... I was feeling very complete')
Despair attributed to an observed entity (looking into Satan's eyes) rather than suffered by the narrator

best_quote.text: It was a void for me, a horrible void, an indescribable, lonely, ugly, horrible feeling.

failure_modes: 'I have been there before' meaning 'I have visited it (in my NDE)' rather than 'it felt already known' — the one systematic semantic slip
Familiarity in ordinary life: Reconnective Healing frequencies, a dream about riding in grandparents' Buick
Post-NDE amnesia where nothing felt familiar (a polarity flip the regex cannot see)
Familiarity of unpleasant earthly sensation on re-entering the body
Past-life confusion ('they were familiar to me, but not as they thought they were')

best_quote.text: I just knew that it was completely familiar and that it wasn't the first time I was there

failure_modes: Colours merely brighter or more vibrant than earth's rather than outside its range ('the colors were more intense', 'a white that dazzled') — 3 passages; these support a weaker claim than the one made
Neuroscience philosophising that colour does not exist in nature at all
An earthly analogy used as the descriptor (Aurora Borealis) with no beyond-range claim
Generalised comparison of 'the other realms' to earth in an after-effects reflection rather than a described perception
Synaesthesia ('the colors were alive', sound bringing colours) rather than impossible hues

best_quote.text: I saw colors that I had never seen before, and I can't describe them, because we don't have the color palette here.

failure_modes: 'Made of light' describing BEINGS — angels, God, an alien, robed figures, orbs — not the shadowless environment. Nine passages, and it is a different (already well-attested) feature of the corpus
Theological inference ('God is light, we're made in his image, so we're made of light')
Interviewer reading the experiencer's own book back to them
'We're made of light and energy' asserted from a hospital bed as general metaphysics
One pure idiom: 'for me I had no shadow' in a story about a job selection process
audits.suggested_regex: (?:there (?:was|were) no (?:sun|shadows?)\b|light (?:was )?everywhere[^.]{0,60}no (?:sun|shadow)|(?:the )?light (?:came|seemed to come|was coming) from (?:with)?in (?:every|each|all)|everything (?:was|is) made of light)

best_quote.text: There was light everywhere but no sun. The light seemed to come from within everything, even the air.

failure_modes: Earthly singing at the bedside — a sister singing a hope song to the patient in hospital
Explicit denials that inherit the vocabulary ('It was nothing like I've read about other people saying, or angels singing')
Other people's experiences (a niece and father who 'described hearing the most beautiful music ever')
A book plug — Don Piper's 90 Minutes in Heaven quoted as the best description of heaven's music
Musical metaphor for non-auditory experience ('like a beautiful harmonic progression' describing weaving vibrations)
Commentary on the purpose of the heavenly choir rather than a description of hearing it

best_quote.text: There was this music that I never heard and never have again that was otherworldly, other instruments, beautiful, all pervasive like this place was music.

failure_modes: The single largest class is the ORDINARY tunnel described as dark — 'a light at the end of this black tunnel', 'traveling down a dark tunnel... I was travelling towards a light'. The classic NDE tunnel is normally dark, so the regex cannot isolate the dark inverse it claims to measure (7 passages)
'Black hole' as a depression metaphor ('the black hole in the pit of my stomach', 'get myself out of this black hole')
'Black hole' as astronomy in a cosmological download, or as a simile for evil beings
'It's like going down the dark tunnel. There ain't no light' used as a simile for looking down a cobra's throat — claim language, zero claim content
A physically dark hospital hallway outside the morgue
Interviewer generalising about the common tunnel motif

A tighter pattern would have to pair the dark shaft with an explicit absence of light or a downward/fire ending; that intersection is rare enough that this node should probably not be built from the current match set

best_quote.text: And I felt like I fell into black. It was all darkness. I was totally alone.

failure_modes: 'Lamb's Book of Life' as scripture, preaching and closing prayer — pure doctrine, never a perceived place (4 passages)
'Akashic Records' as a present-day practice: dice divination, paid readings, psychic sessions, 'I know a couple that work with the Akashic Records'
Generalising about what OTHER NDErs report ('other people who have NDEs sometimes speak of going to a Hall of Records')
Metaphor ('we're different chapters in one book of life') and denial of the building ('I am the freaking Book of Life')
An earthly library in an unrelated vision about a priest's book collection
audits.suggested_regex: (?:I (?:was (?:taken|brought|led)|went|arrived at|found myself in|entered|walked into)[^.]{0,60}(?:hall of (?:records|knowledge|events)|akashic record|library)|(?:a |this |that )(?:vast|enormous|huge|great|endless) library|(?<!Lamb's )books? of life (?:(?:was|were) (?:open|stored)|open))

best_quote.text: My guide communicated to me, this is where the books of life are stored, but we are going to another area.

failure_modes: Direction reversal — the dominant failure. 'I knew everything about the universe / about them / about human evolution' is the experiencer becoming omniscient, the exact inverse of being known (6 passages)

'Nothing was hidden' meaning panoramic 360-degree vision or cosmic transparency, not personal exposure ('there was nothing hidden from me. So while I'm looking to the left, I'm still seeing to the right')
Scripture quotation (Luke 8:17, nothing hidden that will not be revealed)
Speculation about a future heavenly reunion where 'there's nothing to hide'
Ordinary life: a wife who 'knew me better than probably anyone else'
Acceptance or mutual recognition without the knowing (a grandmother who 'knew me very well too')
audits.suggested_regex: (?:(?:he|she|it|they|god|jesus|the light|the being|the presence|this (?:light|being|presence))\s+(?:already )?knew (?:everything|all|it all) about me|I (?:was|felt) (?:completely|totally|fully) known|there was nothing (?:to hide|hidden) from (?:him|her|it|them|god)|they saw (?:every ?(?:bit|thing)|all) of me)

best_quote.text: when he looked into my eyes, he knew everything about me. And he loved me anyway.
